papers.title_en: Sampling at Scale: Distributed Multi-Agent Trajectory Optimization
papers.authors: Minchan Jung, Dimitrios S. Georgiou, Augustinos D. Saravanos, Evangelos A. Theodorou
papers.evidence: 面向大规模智能体团队的分布式多智能体轨迹优化
papers.tldr: 多智能体轨迹优化需兼顾非凸探索与大规模扩展，采样法虽利于探索却受维度限制，分布式集成还面临约束非凸与邻域搜索空间增长的矛盾。本文提出DS-TO，以面向采样的分裂机制让各智能体仅在自身控制空间采样并保持邻域通信，实现完全去中心化并行优化。在2D/3D最多1024智能体任务中，其探索与约束满足优于导数型分布式优化，扩展性优于现有分布式采样方法。
papers.abstract_en: Multi-agent trajectory optimization poses two coupled challenges: effectively exploring non-convex landscapes and scaling favorably to large teams of agents. Sampling-based methods are natural candidates for the exploration challenge but scale poorly with problem dimension. Moreover, their off-the-shelf integration into distributed optimization introduces a fundamental trade-off: sampling either fails to address the constraint-induced non-convexity or its search space grows with neighborhood size. We address this gap by introducing a $\underline{D}\text{istributed}$ $\underline{S}\text{ampling-based}$ $\underline{T}\text{rajectory}$ $\underline{O}\text{ptimization} \ \text{(DS-TO)}$ architecture built on a splitting mechanism tailored to sampling. Under this splitting, each agent samples only in its own control space, independent of neighborhood size, while still remaining exposed to both the constraint-induced non-convexity and the decisions of other agents. The resulting algorithm is fully decentralized, requiring only neighborhood communication, with all local updates executed in parallel across agents. Efficient variations, including parallel Jacobi updates within each agent's subproblem and single-step constraint linearization, further reduce computation. Experiments on 2D and 3D tasks with up to 1024 agents demonstrate improved exploration and constraint satisfaction over state-of-the-art derivative-based distributed optimization, and superior scalability to existing distributed sampling methods.

papers.title_en: MRCT: An Object-Centric Two-Layer Control Architecture for Heavy-Payload Multi-Robot Transportation
papers.authors: Ning Wang, Yoshihiko Nakamura, Tianwei Zhang
papers.evidence: 多机器人协同运输与双层协调控制架构
papers.tldr: 针对异构移动机械臂协同搬运重载时需兼顾载荷运动、接触力分配与柔顺交互的问题，提出以对象为中心的两层控制架构MRCT。上层用MPC为载荷生成协调接触力参考，下层各机器人通过置信度混合速度跟踪与阻抗力矩的WBIC实现该参考。仿真与硬件实验用单臂和双臂移动机械臂搬运接近额定负载的桌子，验证了对象跟踪、接触力调节与姿态稳定。参数敏感性、避障搬运和阶跃负载扰动实验进一步表明该方法在评估条件下可靠有效。
papers.abstract_en: Cooperative transportation of heavy payloads by heterogeneous mobile manipulators requires coordinated payload motion, force distribution, and compliant physical interaction. This paper presents MRCT, an object-centric two-layer control architecture for multi-robot transportation. At the object level, a model predictive controller (MPC) generates a coordinated contact-force reference for the payload. At the robot level, whole- body impedance control (WBIC) modules on individual robots realise the reference through a confidence-based blending of velocity-tracking and impedance torques. The blending mechanism emphasises tracking when the joint-velocity error is small and increases compliance when tracking degrades because of abrupt reference changes or physical disturbances. Simulation and hardware experiments with a heterogeneous team comprising a single-arm and a dual-arm mobile manipulator transporting a near-rated table payload demonstrate accurate object tracking, regulated contact forces, and stable payload orientation. Parameter sensitivity studies, obstacle-avoidance transportation, and step-load disturbance experiments further demonstrate the effectiveness of MRCT for reliable cooperative transportation under the evaluated conditions

papers.title_en: TeamFlowRL: Online Policy Optimization of Decentralized Flow Policies for Multi-Agent Coordination
papers.authors: Guowei Zou, Beiwen Zhang, Haitao Wang, Hong Hong, Zhiquan Chen, Hejun Wu
papers.evidence: 面向多智能体协调的去中心化策略在线优化
papers.tldr: 多智能体协作任务需要协调一致的行为，离线生成式策略虽能从轨迹中学到表达能力强的协作行为，却受限于固定数据集。TeamFlowRL提出两阶段框架：先离线预训练去中心化流策略，再在线微调，并在完整去噪轨迹上优化团队策略以避开难以计算的动作似然。在七组仿真共51个配对配置上，它提升了所有离线初始化，归一化得分平均提升47.3%。
papers.abstract_en: Complex cooperative tasks require coordinated multi-agent behavior. Offline generative policies learn expressive cooperative behaviors from trajectories but remain limited by fixed datasets. Online reinforcement learning can improve them through environment interaction. However, fine-tuning flow policies is difficult because action likelihoods are hard to compute. We propose TeamFlowRL, a two-stage framework that pretrains multi-agent flow policies offline and fine-tunes them online. We formulate team policy optimization over the complete denoising trajectories of decentralized flow policies, avoiding intractable action likelihoods. The resulting objective weights each agent's trajectory ratio with a shared team advantage and clips each ratio separately, aligning local policy updates with the common team return. Across 51 paired configurations in seven simulation groups, TeamFlowRL improves every offline initialization, with a 47.3% average gain in normalized score. It also achieves 33.1% higher average success under exploration noise than Gaussian-policy fine-tuning across 6 bimanual tasks.

papers.title_en: Beyond Easy Clients: Difficulty- and Improvement-Aware Aggregation for Federated Reinforcement Learning in Robot Navigation
papers.authors: Ye Lin Tun, Chu Myaet Thwal, Eui-Nam Huh, Choong Seon Hong
papers.evidence: 面向机器人车队的联邦学习导航协调
papers.tldr: 联邦强化学习让机器人集群在不交换原始经验的前提下共同学习导航策略，但各客户端环境难度差异大，统一平均聚合会给已“饱和”的简单客户端过高权重。论文提出FedDIA，以客户端本地训练对全局模型的改进幅度乘以环境难度来打分，两个信号都相对全局模型测量因而可比。在八个异构客户端的地图无关导航任务上，成功率75.5%，优于最强基线68.7%，并在迁移到仓库与居住空间布局及存在缺陷客户端时保持优势。
papers.abstract_en: Federated reinforcement learning enables a fleet of robots to jointly learn a shared navigation policy without exchanging raw experience. In practice, however, the robots rarely operate in the same conditions: an open aisle is far easier to navigate than a cluttered room, and takes less learning to master. Standard federated aggregation rules ignore this. Uniform averaging weights every client equally, whether or not it is still learning, and weighting by episode return is worse, since easy environments permit high returns by construction. Both failures stem from what we call the \emph{plateau problem}: once a client masters its environment, its updates carry little new information even though its reported return remains high. We propose \emph{FedDIA}, which scores each client by how much its local training improves the global model it received, amplified by the difficulty of its environment. Difficulty is inferred from the model's own performance, without requiring any description of the environment. Both signals are measured against the global model, so they are comparable across clients. On a mapless navigation task with eight heterogeneous clients, FedDIA reaches a mean success rate of $75.5\%$ across training and held-out environments, against $68.7\%$ for the strongest federated baseline. Its advantage holds when the models are transferred to hand-authored warehouse and living-space layouts, or when one of the clients is defective.

papers.title_en: DeCoNav-Act: Benchmarking Collective Physical Capability in Multi-Robot Mobile Manipulation
papers.authors: Yunzi Wu, Sunyao Zhou, Xiaotao Zhang, Yucheng Deng, Yuehao Huang, Lin Qian, Xuanrui Cui, Xinhai Li, Chenjia Bai, Hongqing Chu, Xuelong Li
papers.evidence: 语言引导的多机器人协同移动操作基准
papers.tldr: 现有多机器人基准多关注任务分配与技能排序，却很少检验共享物理状态是否可供队友使用。DeCoNav-Act 在共享物理仿真中构建语言引导的多机器人移动操作基准，含350个同构与150个异构任务，覆盖并行负载和物理依赖两类协作。它除团队成功率外还评测路径效率、交接覆盖率与成功率，并用已验证的交接前状态做诊断。实验显示现有方法在GPT-5.6-luna下无一完成任务，在GPT-6.1-sol下CoMoMa仅26.5%建立条件、4.1%成功。
papers.abstract_en: Robot teams can split workloads or combine complementary bodies, but only if each robot leaves the shared world in a state its teammate can use. Existing multi-robot benchmarks emphasize task allocation and skill sequencing, rarely testing whether the resulting physical states are usable. To evaluate collective physical capability, we introduce DeCoNav-Act, a benchmark for language-guided multi-robot mobile manipulation in a shared physics simulation. Its 350 homogeneous and 150 heterogeneous tasks, each verified by joint reference execution, span two coordination mechanisms: parallel workloads in shared space and physical dependencies in which one robot establishes a condition for a teammate to use. Beyond team success, DeCoNav-Act measures path efficiency and handoff coverage and success, and adds a diagnostic from verified pre-handoff states. Evaluating sensor-grounded adaptations of ASPIRE and RAX and our agent CoMoMa, we find that with GPT-5.6-luna no method completes a task, at most 8.8% of dependencies are reached, and even from pre-handoff states no handoff is completed; with GPT-6.1-sol, CoMoMa establishes the condition in 26.5% of trials, but only 4.1% succeed.

papers.title_en: MRBench: Benchmarking Physical Necessity Reasoning in Heterogeneous Multi-Robot Manipulation
papers.authors: Yanzhe Chen, Zhijun Cao, Ruihe An, Chang Gong, Mike Zheng Shou
papers.evidence: 异构多机器人操作协调基准
papers.tldr: 多机器人协作成功并不等于真正理解哪些机器人不可或缺；当机器人能力、资源可用性或可替代物体变化时，任务所需团队也会改变。作者提出MRBench，包含8类并发与可达约束任务及5种资源变化配置，系统评测异构多机器人操作中的物理必要性推理。并提出MRScissors，将任务需求与实测物理能力分离，通过约束搜索识别最小可行团队。其团队选择准确率达85.4%和91.2%，较最强基线提升10.4和9.5点，揭示协调能力与必要性理解之间的关键缺口。
papers.abstract_en: Recent advances in multi-robot manipulation have shown how robots can collaborate to accomplish complex tasks. However, successful coordination does not reveal which robots are actually needed. The same task may require different teams as robot capabilities change, resources become unavailable, or objects replace robotic support. We argue that reliable multi-robot manipulation requires physical necessity reasoning: understanding what a task demands, which resources can fulfill those demands, and which are truly necessary. We introduce MRBench, a benchmark for physical necessity reasoning in heterogeneous multi-robot manipulation. It comprises eight tasks with distinct concurrency and reach constraints, each evaluated under five configurations that change the required resources while preserving the task goal. Our evaluation reveals that existing coordination agents perform well with reference teams but struggle when robot embodiments change or passive objects can replace robotic support. To address this gap, we propose MRScissors, which separates task requirements from measured physical capabilities and identifies minimal feasible teams through constrained search. Across two model backbones, MRScissors achieves 85.4% and 91.2% team-selection accuracy, outperforming the strongest baselines by 10.4 and 9.5 points, respectively. Together, these findings expose a critical gap between coordinating robots and understanding their physical necessity.
